summary: The legacy runners are unreachable from both live commands, but their declarations are co-located with live helpers and package-wide types. No production Go file is a certified standalone deletion unit on this base. Phase A must extract the live surfaces, collapse the duplicate catalog, forbid new imports into the legacy packages, and defer full deletion until the ported tests and full cross-platform gates prove a bounded removal.

stale_forgejo_workflow.disposition: separate bounded cleanup after confirming Forgejo is no longer an active required CI surface

removal_probes.reason: bridge.Main shares its file with live NormalizePeerName and QwenNativeSessionTitle plus package-wide legacy helpers
RunAgent shares its file and private agent type with embedded/registration/lane code while live launchers consume status/runtime helpers
RunHub owns types used by legacy lane routing and is still called by same-package and command integration tests

bounded_deletion.reason: Every legacy runner declaration is file-entangled; production commands still expose 32 bridge symbols, live command/launcher code consumes federator registration and diagnostics, and the old RunAgent/RunHub remain test roots. Making a broad deletion pass known gates would require simultaneous helper extraction, test porting, and package reshaping, which would put the six-product critical path at risk. Deadcode counts are prioritization evidence, not file-deletion proof.

fail-loud product labeling in place of the unknown-to-Claude default

mechanism: capture this inventory as the baseline allowlist
add a go/parser conformance test that rejects any new direct import of internal/bridge or internal/federator outside the temporary explicit allowlist
shrink the allowlist on every extraction
ban package-init registration and duplicate product tables in scripts/test
require productcatalog projection equality after deleting internal/federator/product.go

uncertainty: Deadcode is a sound RTA result for each recorded GOOS/GOARCH command, but it does not by itself certify deletion of types, variables, initializers, interface-only methods, tests, or entire files.
The scanner records syntactic selector references; references inside unreachable bridge functions are intentionally retained as conservative extraction candidates until Phase A moves the live roots.

Only Linux/amd64 and Darwin/arm64 were compared in this spike; the released amd64/arm64 variants share source families, but any later deletion still requires the full four-platform build and physical release gates.
The Forgejo workflow is source-stale, but whether the Forgejo service remains organizationally required is outside static Go reachability.
follow_up_deletion_gate: all live external roots have focused-package replacements
no production importer remains for internal/bridge or legacy internal/federator surfaces
legacy command tests are ported to internal/federation and unified daemon fixtures
cross-platform deadcode/call inventory identifies a closed file set
normal, race, vet, lint, federation, focused contracts, prebuilt install, quickstart, owner-nonmutation, and physical macOS gates pass
deletion lands as a standalone reviewable change rather than mixed with a product adapter
